audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phases[0..2].side and phases[4].side all read "Skill" while the content layer win[0..2] and win[4] read "Orianna". Four rows rendered two different answers.
audit.why: Mel is a squishy 950-range mage who must step up to stack Overwhelm and whose only defensive tool, Rebuttal, is on 38s at rank 1 - Orianna's placed ball out-ranges and out-shoves her through levels 1-3. At 6 the row stays Orianna because Golden Eclipse cashes Overwhelm stacks and needs you low, which the 9s E shield prevents.
audit.corrected: phases[0..2].side -> Orianna (7/10) and phases[4].side -> Orianna (6/10), matching the content layer and the packet levelChart; whys rewritten in the same proposal.

audit.why: Spike placement holds: Orianna's Lost Chapter trade window, Mel's level 6 Golden Eclipse (120/100/80, global range), a shared first-item poke spike, and Orianna's late five-man Shockwave against Mel's single-target execute.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction - Rebuttal's cooldown - was never given a number, and dosFull[2].d asserted a fifteen-second window that exists nowhere in the kit.
audit.why: Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26s. It reflects projectiles (your Q is flagged projectile) and prevents her taking damage at all, so the whole matchup is baiting one long cooldown. Searing Brilliance gives her three bonus projectiles per ability cast, up to nine, on her next attack - the wind-up after a cast is the burst tell, not the cast itself. Solar Snare is an 1000-range root on 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s and is her only all-in setup.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0..2] and dontsFull[0] now carry the real 38s/26s Rebuttal numbers, the 11s Snare, and the bait-then-commit sequence.
sources: brief enemyKit P Searing Brilliance text

audit.whatIsWrong: Twenty-eight lint findings on this matchup, twenty-five of them misgendering: Mel was called he/his/him across tldr, winCon, tradeGood, tradeBad, six phases whys, breakdown.wave, breakdown.trading, five dos/donts fields and five report entries.
audit.why: champ-data/champ-gender.js lists mel as female. The owner is addressed as "you", so every third-person pronoun on the page refers to Mel.
audit.corrected: All flagged fields rewritten with she/her. The report entries are corrected as pronoun swaps only, not rewrites, to stay inside the report-scope limit.

audit.whatIsWrong: The brief's missingInteractions proposes a "terrain-cuts-retreat" line saying Mel can wall off your escape with Rebuttal.
audit.why: Riot's own W text describes a barrier around herself that reflects projectiles, prevents damage and grants movement speed - no wall, no terrain. The kit file's terrain flag is a tooltip-parsing misfire, so that headline was NOT written to the page.
audit.corrected: No edit. The autoreset-burst-tell headline is genuine and is reflected in the audit above; the terrain claim is discarded.

notes: The brief's missingInteractions block asks for a terrain line - that Mel can cut your retreat with Rebuttal. Riot's own W text says it is a barrier around herself (reflect, damage immunity, movement speed) with no wall, so the kit file's terrain flag is a parsing misfire and that line was deliberately NOT written. Cross-layer chart disagreement fixed on rows 0,1,2,4 (full said Skill, content said Orianna, packet agreed with content); no paired win[N] edits are proposed because win[N] already holds the correct value on disk. report[3].t, report[4].t and report[11].t also carry misgendered pronouns but are composed of the tradeGood/tradeBad/wave/donts strings this proposal is already rewriting - they were left for the applier to keep consistent rather than burning report-scope on three more rewrites; if the applier does not propagate, they need a follow-up pronoun pass. Whether Rebuttal reflects Shockwave specifically is not in the kit - the page now says only that she takes no damage through it, which the text does state.
